Leni Robredo’s competence as a lawyer is often viewed through the lens of developmental and human rights law rather than high-stakes corporate litigation. While her critics sometimes point to her passing the Bar exam on her second attempt, her supporters and peers emphasize her decade-long dedication to grassroots legal work.  

Here is a breakdown of her legal career and the context of her professional reputation:
1️⃣ Focus on Marginalized Communities
Robredo is widely recognized for her work in "alternative law," which focuses on empowering the poor rather than just winning cases in a courtroom.
• Public Attorney’s Office (PAO): She served in the PAO in Naga City, providing free legal services to indigent litigants.  
• SALIGAN: For over a decade (1998–2008), she was the Bicol coordinator for Sentro ng Alternatibong Lingap Panligal (SALIGAN). Her work involved traveling to remote areas to provide legal aid to farmers, fisherfolk, and indigenous peoples.  
• Paralegal Training: Instead of just litigating, she focused on teaching communities about their rights so they could advocate for themselves, a hallmark of "developmental" lawyering.
  
2️⃣ Legislative Track Record
During her time in the House of Representatives (2013–2016), she translated her legal background into policy. Her legal competence was reflected in her focus on transparency and institutional reform:  
• Tax Incentives Management and Transparency Act (TIMTA): She was a principal author of this law (RA 10708), which aimed to hold government spending on tax incentives accountable.  
• Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act: She co-authored this law, which notably includes the first anti-political dynasty provision in Philippine history.  

3️⃣ Professional Standing and Recognition
• Peer Respect: She has been invited to speak at Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) conventions, where she has challenged lawyers to use their skills to protect the Constitution and the disenfranchised.  
• Academic and International Recognition: Her legal and public service background contributed to her selection as a Hauser Leader at Harvard Kennedy School in 2022, where she lectured on leadership and public policy.  

Track record of Sara Duterte! 

1️⃣ The Impeachment Battles (2025–2026)
This is the defining scandal of her term. She made history in February 2025 by becoming the first Philippine Vice President to be impeached by the House of Representatives.  
 
2️⃣ The "Assassination Threat" Controversy
In late 2024, during a late-night press briefing, Duterte made a statement that she had hired an assassin to kill President Bongbong Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and Speaker Martin Romualdez if she herself were to be killed.  

3️⃣ Misuse of Confidential Funds
This remains her most persistent scandal. Investigations by the Commission on Audit (COA) and Congress revealed:
• The 11-Day Spend: The OVP allegedly spent ₱125 million in confidential funds in just 11 days in December 2022.  
• DepEd Spending: During her time as Education Secretary, she requested and spent hundreds of millions in confidential funds that critics argue should have gone toward classrooms and teacher salaries.  
• Result: For the 2026 National Budget, the Office of the Vice President has been allocated zero confidential funds.  
4️⃣ Ties to Apollo Quiboloy
Her close relationship with the self-proclaimed "Appointed Son of God," Apollo Quiboloy, has become a liability.
  
5️⃣ The ICC & "War on Drugs"
While the International Criminal Court (ICC) case primarily targets her father, Rodrigo Duterte, Sara is increasingly linked to the investigation.
• The ICC recently (January 2026) ruled that Rodrigo Duterte is fit to stand trial for crimes against humanity.  
• Sara’s alleged involvement in the "Davao Death Squad" during her time as Mayor of Davao City is a secondary focus of the ICC's broader probe into the drug war.

data.text:
Please pray – persecuted believers amongst families devastated by fire.

Last week, a massive fire swept through a community in southern Philippines, destroying 40 homes and displacing 60 families. Thankfully, no lives have been lost, but several people have been injured.

Those affected include Christian families who already face a great deal of pressure and isolation for their faith. The picture shows a Christian woman and her two children standing in the ashes of what was once their home.

“Our hearts are heavy. The fire was so fast, and now so many have nothing left,” shares a local partner. 

“Among those who lost their homes are 13 families from our community, including our persecuted believers. They are exhausted and traumatised. This is not the first time they have lost everything. We are doing what we can, but the need is overwhelming.”

Please pray
- That all those affected will be provided with food, water, clothing, shelter and other necessities 
- For the peace of Jesus to guard the minds of believers and for them to know the comfort that only He can bring
- That the local authorities will respond with compassion and urgency to the needs of all those affected by this fire.

profile_bio.description: Supporting persecuted Christians who dare to follow Jesus no matter the cost.
